about.home.welcome.title: What it is
about.home.welcome.body: Heroquill helps you build, play and print Dungeons & Dragons 5th edition characters with the SRD 5.1 rules. It is free, needs no account, works offline once opened, and keeps your characters on this device.
about.home.flow.title: How it works
about.home.flow.body: Create guides you step by step: origin, class, ability scores, choices, spells, equipment and story. Sheet shows the finished character, Play is for the table (hit points, rests, spell slots, rolls) and Print makes paper or PDF. Free edit lets you override any number, and Level up is in Create and in Play.
about.home.share.title: Sharing and backup
about.home.share.body: Share makes a link, a QR code or a file that opens the character on another device. Export saves a character as a file and Import brings it back. Characters live only in this browser, so export them to keep a copy.
about.home.packs.title: Content packs
about.home.packs.body: Write your own homebrew with the editor (spells, items, feats, species, backgrounds, classes, subclasses), or add content from other tools: Aurora XML files, an index file or an address. What you add stays on your device. A pack made from files you imported can be removed but not exported or shared.
about.home.translation.title: Languages and translation
about.home.translation.body: The app speaks English, Italian, French, German and Spanish. The rules texts come from the official SRD translations; the few that are missing show in English. With your own DeepL key, Automatic translation translates them as you read and marks them. Distances follow the language, and can be changed at the top.
about.home.beta.title: This version
about.home.beta.body: Version {version}. It works, but it still needs a lot of testing: if something looks wrong, a number does not add up or a text is missing, tell us.
about.roadmap.intro: What is still missing, from the nearest to the furthest.
about.changelog.intro: What changed in each version, newest first.
translate.title: Automatic translation
translate.intro: Texts that have no translation in your language yet are translated as you read them, for free and with nothing to set up. A translated text says so, and can be switched back to the English original. Translations are kept on this device, so each text is translated only once.
translate.english: Nothing to translate while the app is in English. Choose another language first.
translate.enable: Translate the texts that are still in English
translate.descOnlyHint: Machine translation does well with sentences and badly with a name on its own: without context, a name often comes out wrong. With this on, names stay in English and everything else is translated. It also uses fewer of your characters.
translate.keyHint: With your own DeepL key the translations are better. A free key (it ends in :fx) or a paid one, from your DeepL account. It stays on this device and travels to DeepL, through the relay, with each request. Without it the free translation is used.
translate.howTo: How to get a DeepL key
translate.howTo1: Make a free account for the DeepL API (not the ordinary translator app) at
translate.howTo2: Open your account and go to the API Keys tab: there is a key, ending in :fx if the plan is free.
translate.howTo3: Copy it and paste it in the box above. That is all.
translate.howToNote: The free plan has an allowance of characters, which DeepL may change; the page above says how much. A game's texts use little of it, and what is translated is kept on this device, so nothing is paid for twice.
translate.relayHint: DeepL does not accept requests straight from a web page, so they go through a small relay. The default one is run by the author of the app; it keeps neither your key nor your texts, and its code is in the repository. You can run your own: see
translate.clearConfirm: Delete {n} saved translations? They are translated again when needed.
translate.upgradeHint: A text translated by a weaker engine (when the better ones were not available) is translated again, by the best one you have, when you read it. Only what you read is translated again.
translate.advanced: Advanced: your own DeepL key and relay
translate.err.unreachable: The relay could not be reached. Check its address and your connection.
translate.err.refused: DeepL refused the key. Check that it is complete.
translate.err.limit: Too many requests at once. Wait a moment and open the text again.
translate.err.quota: The allowance of translations is used up for today. Try again tomorrow, or use your own DeepL key.

credits.title: Credits and licenses
credits.rulesIntro: The rules text and data come from the System Reference Document, used under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license.
credits.dataText: The structured SRD data is derived from the 5e-database project (MIT License).
credits.translationsText: Translated rules texts come from the official translations of the SRD 5.1 published by Wizards of the Coast under the same Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license. They have been matched to the structured data by this project.
credits.designText: The layout of the character sheet and its set of pages (main sheet, story, feature cards, spell cards) are inspired by the class character sheets by Emmet Byrne. All artwork in this app is drawn from scratch; no artwork from those sheets is used.

tour.welcome.title: Welcome to Heroquill
tour.welcome.body: A short tour of what the app can do, about a minute. You can leave at any time, and take it again from the ☰ menu.
tour.characters.title: Your characters
tour.characters.body: Every character is saved on this device as you work: nothing to press and no account. Here you switch between characters or start a new one.
tour.more.title: Backup, share, move
tour.more.body: The ⋯ menu duplicates a character, exports it to a file, backs up all of them, moves everything to another device, shares it or imports one. Make a backup from time to time: the data lives only on this device.
tour.tabs.title: Five tabs
tour.tabs.body: Build creates the character, Sheet reads it, Play is for the table, Rules is the SRD to browse and Print makes the paper sheet or a PDF.
tour.build.title: Build, step by step
tour.build.body: Start with species and background, then class, ability scores, choices, spells and equipment. The steps open one at a time, and a note tells what is still left to do.
tour.summary.title: The numbers, live
tour.summary.body: Armor class, hit points, initiative and ability scores change with every choice you make. Once the character has a class, a button here raises its level.
tour.sheet.title: The sheet
tour.sheet.body: The whole character, worked out: abilities, skills, saving throws, attacks, spells, features and story. Many numbers can be tapped to see how they are worked out.
tour.play.title: Play at the table
tour.play.body: Hit points, conditions, rests, spell slots and resources to keep track of, and dice for every roll: tap a skill or an attack to roll it, with advantage or disadvantage.
tour.rules.title: The rules at hand
tour.rules.body: Search the whole SRD 5.1: spells, items, classes, species and more, in your language. Press / from anywhere to come straight here.
tour.print.title: Print or save as a PDF
tour.print.body: Choose what goes on paper (the sheet, spell cards, the story), the paper size and a low-ink mode, then print or save a PDF.
tour.search.title: Search from anywhere
tour.search.body: This button, or the / key, opens the search of the rules.
tour.menu.title: Menu: language, look and more
tour.menu.body: Language, colour set, light or dark mode and units are here, with the content packs (your own or from Aurora files), the homebrew editor, automatic translation and the credits.
tour.end.title: You are ready
tour.end.body: That is all. Build a character, or open the example, Aria, to look around. The guides on the website go deeper, and this tour is always in the ☰ menu.

tour.packs.title: Your own content
tour.packs.body: Content packs is where you add what the SRD does not include: your homebrew, or Aurora files you already have. Choose files or an index file, or paste the address of one here. Everything stays on this device.
tour.translate.title: Automatic translation
tour.translate.body: Texts with no translation in your language are translated as you read, for free. For better quality you can paste your own DeepL key here (a free one works): DeepL reads more naturally than the free service, and the key stays on this device. The guide on the website shows how to get one.
